parent.title: Which Linux to switch to in 2026: a decision framework for a .NET developer leaving Windows

siblings.title: The 2026 Linux distro landscape: what actually differs between the families
siblings.summary: There are only five real distro families, and for a Windows developer moving to Linux in 2026 the honest shortlist is Fedora Workstation, Ubuntu LTS, Linux Mint, Bluefin/Aurora, and openSUSE Tumbleweed — everything else is a variation, a server OS, or a hobby.

siblings.title: Stable, rolling, or atomic: picking a release model for your first Linux daily driver
siblings.summary: Start on a 6-month fixed release (Fedora Workstation) or an atomic Fedora image (Bluefin DX); avoid pure rolling and avoid Debian stable.

siblings.title: Toolchain fit: which Linux distro costs least setup work for .NET 10 + TypeScript + Docker in 2026
siblings.summary: For a .NET 10 + TypeScript + Docker workstation in 2026, Ubuntu 26.04 LTS and Fedora 44 tie on setup effort and every other family costs you at least one hand-configured vendor repo.

siblings.title: Picking a Linux desktop in 2026: the Windows 11 switcher's decision guide
siblings.summary: KDE Plasma is the lowest-friction landing spot for a Windows 11 developer in 2026; X11 sessions die this year.

siblings.title: Hardware and driver reality in 2026: only three things should decide your distro
siblings.summary: In 2026 only three hardware classes still force a distro choice — NVIDIA, very new silicon, and Secure-Boot dual-boot.

siblings.title: Windows to Linux in 2026: what crosses over, what doesn't, and how to stage the switch
siblings.summary: Almost everything a .NET developer does crosses to Linux in 2026 — the four things that don't are desktop Office with VBA, a native Outlook with working calendar, WPF/WinForms designers, and Windows-only compliance tooling.

siblings.title: Linux upkeep in 2026: support windows, upgrade pain, and monthly chores ranked
siblings.summary: Atomic Fedora and Ubuntu/Mint LTS are near-zero chore; Fedora Workstation costs one upgrade a year; Arch costs a reading habit you cannot skip.

siblings.title: Gaming and media on Linux in 2026: singleplayer is solved, anti-cheat and DRM streaming are not
siblings.summary: Roughly 90% of Windows Steam titles launch under Proton; the two real losses are kernel anti-cheat multiplayer and browser DRM streaming above 720p SDR.

sources.title: Plasma 6.7 release announcement (kde.org)
sources.claim: Plasma 6.7 (16 June 2026) adds per-screen virtual desktops, simultaneous ICC colour management plus HDR, and performance/power improvements.

sources.title: xdg-desktop-portal discussion #1368
sources.claim: KDE is effectively the only desktop with a working GlobalShortcuts portal backend; GNOME 50 has none functional and xdg-desktop-portal-wlr ships no implementation.

sources.title: GNOME 50 extension review status (discourse.gnome.org)

sources.title: Linux Mint Wayland fully supported (OMG! Ubuntu)

sources.title: X11 on GNOME is finally dead (XDA)
sources.claim: GNOME 50 removed the X11 session entirely (about 27,540 lines cut from Mutter).

sources.title: Cinnamon Wayland is good (Phoronix)
sources.claim: Cinnamon's Wayland session is no longer experimental; Mint developers describe it as almost on par with X11.

sources.title: Xfce Wayland compositor first preview (Linuxiac)
sources.claim: Xfce's Wayland compositor xfwl4 reached first preview on 22 June 2026 and still has bugs and missing features.

sources.title: Xfce Wayland roadmap (wiki.xfce.org)

sources.title: 10 best Linux desktop environments (linuxblog.io)
sources.claim: 2026 idle memory measurements rank XFCE lightest (~1.36 GB), then Cinnamon (~1.89 GB), GNOME (~2.10 GB), KDE Plasma (~2.67 GB).

sources.title: KDE VDG gestures (community.kde.org)
sources.claim: KDE exposes configurable three- and four-finger touchpad gesture bindings in System Settings on Wayland.

sources.title: GNOME 50 release notes
sources.claim: GNOME 50 enables fractional scaling and VRR by default, improves NVIDIA performance, and accelerates Remote Desktop.

sources.title: Configure the touchpad and gestures (linuxjunkies.org)
sources.claim: GNOME supports three-finger swipe workspace switching out of the box on Wayland.

sources.title: Cinnamon 6.8 will fully support Wayland (9to5Linux)
sources.claim: Cinnamon 6.8 adds improved multi-monitor support, hardware acceleration and full HiDPI to its Wayland session.

sources.title: Desktop environment comparison (eylenburg.github.io)
sources.claim: GNOME and Plasma support HDR and VRR while Xfce and Cinnamon support neither; per-DE RAM within ~60 MB of each other.

sources.title: Wayland and Sway in 2026 (Michael Stapelberg)
sources.claim: On Sway: single-window sharing broken, XWayland not scaled, Chrome GPU process dies after resize, MST monitors appear as two screens.

sources.title: Hyprland vs niri vs i3 vs Sway (MakeUseOf)
sources.claim: niri best for laptop-first scrollable workflows, Sway most predictable, Hyprland best eye candy with faster churn.

sources.title: niri (gvolpe.com)
sources.claim: niri arranges windows in an infinite horizontal scrolling strip per workspace.

sources.title: Electron issue #30652 — redundant Wayland share dialog
sources.claim: Electron apps such as Slack show a redundant duplicate screen-share picker on Wayland and may need the WebRTCPipeWireCapturer flag.

sources.title: Zoom: sharing on Wayland works only the first time
sources.claim: On Wayland, Zoom's first screen share works but a second attempt produces a black screen.

sources.title: org.freedesktop.portal.GlobalShortcuts docs

sources.title: Clipboard manager Wayland support issues (BigGo)

sources.title: Remote desktop options for headless Plasma (Manjaro forum)
sources.claim: KRDP shares only an already-logged-in Plasma session with no headless support; GNOME/GDM supports remote login and headless sessions.

sources.title: KWin lands explicit sync (Phoronix)
sources.claim: Explicit sync on NVIDIA requires Xwayland 24.1+, KWin 6.1+ and NVIDIA drivers 555.58 or newer.

sources.title: NVIDIA 580 on KDE Wayland freezes (NVIDIA forums)

sources.title: Hacker News discussion on Wayland in 2026
